entry.title: The Evolution of the SAP User Interface: From SAP GUI to Fiori to Joule Work
entry.content:
The Evolution of the SAP User Interface: From SAP GUI to Fiori to Joule Work

From transactions to intuitive apps to AI-powered collaboration – the SAP user experience is not just changing its appearance. It is changing the way we work.

Anyone who has worked with SAP for a long time will remember it: the classic SAP GUI, countless transaction codes, complex screens, and a user interface that was primarily designed to do one thing – provide functionality.

But the world has changed. And so have our expectations of enterprise software.

Looking back, we can see just how far we have come – and what this evolution means for us as people.

1. SAP GUI – The Era of Transactions

Throughout the 1990s and well beyond, SAP GUI was the central entry point to business processes in countless companies.

The interface was powerful, stable, and designed to support complex business processes. To use SAP efficiently, users had to become familiar with transaction codes, screens, fields, and process logic.

People had to learn how SAP worked.

Over the years, experienced users developed an enormous amount of knowledge. They knew which transaction to use, which fields mattered, and which steps were required to achieve the desired result.

It worked – but shift began in the design of the user experience.

Instead of complex transaction screens, the focus moved towards role-based apps, modern design, and more intuitive interaction. The user experience became increasingly aligned with people's tasks and needs.

Information was meant to be easier to access. Processes were meant to become more understandable. And SAP was increasingly expected to feel as intuitive as the modern applications we use in everyday life.

The key question changed: Not just “How does this transaction work?” but “What task do I want to accomplish?”

With Fiori, access to SAP became more modern, flexible, and better suited to different roles and devices.

This was more than a new design. It was an important step towards a better user experience and a stronger focus on people.

3. Joule Work – From Using Software to AI-Powered Collaboration

With generative AI, the next chapter of the SAP user experience is beginning.

AI assistants such as Joule make it possible to ask for information in natural language, understand relationships more quickly, and receive intelligent support when completing certain tasks.

With Joule Work, SAP is taking this approach further towards an AI-powered work environment. The aim is to bring information and work contexts together more effectively and support tasks across different applications and business processes.

Instead of navigating exclusively through menus and applications, users can increasingly describe what they want to achieve.

Imagine a typical business scenario:

Instead of opening multiple reports and manually compiling data, a user could ask:

“Analyze sales performance over the past three months, identify the largest deviations, and summarize the most important areas for action.”

The vision is for AI to help users find information, analyze data, and prepare decisions – and, depending on available capabilities and permissions, also assist in executing tasks.

People will spend less time searching for information and more time interpreting it and making the right decisions.

An important point: Not every task can already be fully automated. The actual benefits depend on the available capabilities, integration with business processes, and the quality of the underlying data.

4. The Real Change Is About People

The evolution of the SAP user interface is therefore not just a story about technology.

It is also a story about how our work is changing.

Era What matters most What it means for people

SAP GUITransactions and screensSystem knowledge and process expertise are essential
SAP FioriApps and tasksMore intuitive interaction and easier access to information
Joule Work and AIIntent, context, and assistanceGreater focus on analysis, decisions, and collaboration

This evolution raises important questions.

Which skills will become more important in the future?

Knowledge of individual transactions will remain valuable in many areas. At the same time, other skills will become increasingly important: asking the right questions, critically evaluating results, understanding business processes, and using AI effectively.

The roles of IT departments, SAP consultants, and process owners are also changing. It is no longer just about configuring systems correctly and training users. Increasingly, it is about designing intelligent workflows, making meaningful use of data, and helping people adapt to a new world of work.

And this is where a major challenge lies: New technology alone does not change the way people work. Real value is created only when people understand, trust, and use it effectively.

5. What Does This Mean for SAP Transformations?

For companies, one important insight emerges: The evolution of the user interface should not be treated as an isolated IT project.

Organizations modernizing SAP should also rethink their workflows, employee roles, data quality, and opportunities for automation.

Some key questions to consider:

  • Which tasks can be simplified through better user experience and guidance?

  • Where can AI assistants make information available more quickly?

  • Which processes are suitable for further automation?

  • How can we ensure that employees understand and embrace the new possibilities?

  • How do we measure whether productivity, quality, and employee satisfaction are actually improving?

Especially in the SAP ecosystem, it will be crucial to develop technology, processes, and people together.

Because a modern interface is not an end in itself. It must make work easier, better, and more meaningful.

Conclusion: Less Time Operating Systems. More Time Making an Impact.

From SAP GUI through SAP Fiori to Joule Work, we are witnessing an evolution that goes far beyond the design of a user interface.

We are moving from a world where people had to learn how to operate the system, through a world of intuitive, task-oriented applications, towards a way of working in which AI increasingly understands, assists, and supports tasks.

The exciting question is therefore no longer just what the next SAP interface will look like.

The real question is: How much more can people achieve when technology takes some of the complexity off their shoulders?

The future of SAP will not be measured solely by how intelligent the systems become. It will be measured by how effectively they help people make better decisions, collaborate more efficiently, and focus on what truly matters.

Less complexity. More intelligence. More time for what really matters.

#SAP #SAPFiori #Joule #JouleWork #SAPTransformation #AI #UserExperience #DigitalTransformation

entry.title: How to run SAC Pull integration Job from SAP Analytics Cloud Multi Action using API_FINPLANPULLJOB
entry.content:
Introduction

The purpose of this post is to introduce a new service API_FINPLANPULLJOB that was recently included into Communication Scenario SAP_COM_0087 of SAP S/4HANA Public Cloud. This service provides a convenient and tailored mechanism for planner to start integration jobs between SAP Analytics Cloud and SAP S/4HANA Cloud on the direction to S/4HANA by simple click directly from SAC Story using Multi Action.

It provides an alternative, but more direct way to start integration compared to manual start from S/4HANA Fiori application "Schedule Financial Plan Data Jobs". 

The new service is an alternative (so far only for Cloud customers) to the old approach of triggering integration jobs with generic service BC_EXT_APPJOB_MANAGEMENT as it was previously described in the Blog post.

The new service is supporting target types of ACDOCP, FINSSKF, ACCOSTRATE and CCFCTR.

To get scenario working, some configuration steps are required: starting with configuring users on SAP S/4HANA side, followed by creating HTTP API connection on SAP Analytics Cloud side, and, finally, configuring Multi Action in SAC Story.

In this scenario it is important to understand that three types of S/4HANA users are involved in the process:
    - Communication user;
    - Business user for posting plan data ("posting" user);
    - Business user for monitoring application jobs and application logs ("monitoring" user).

A communication user is only used to call the needed S/4HANA inbound service (API_FINPLANPULLJOB) from SAC tenant, whereas the "posting" user is bearing all necessary authorizations for integrating data to respective target tables, for example, ACDOCP. Even though the whole process is triggered by SAC using the communication user, the actual integration Job gets started on behalf of "posting" user. After the job is finished, it collects application logs in the system. This log "belongs" to communication user and by-default for security reasons is not available for reading by any other S/4HANA user. Therefore, we need a third type of user – "monitoring user" which has extra authorization to see application logs of other S/4HANA users, i.e. to read logs created by communication user. The "posting" and "monitoring" can technically be the same S/4HANA user.

The following block-diagram provides a conceptual view on service architecture:

The following flow diagram describes an example of typical process, starting from pressing "Multi Action Starter" button in your Story, invoking all three types of endpoints, until a final message toast is displayed on the screen:

As a preparation to further configuration, you have to maintain these three users in the SAP S/4HANA client and grant each user the respective authorizations.

Prerequisite

Make sure that scope items 1YB and 1HB are active.

Settings for S/4HANA Public Cloud

1) Create communication user using App "Maintain Communication Users" (App ID F1338).

2) Create two communication systems for communication scenarios SAP_COM_0087 and SAP_COM_0326 and two communication arrangements respectively. The key requirement here is to specify the same communication user in the mentioned artifacts.

2.a) Use App "Communication Systems" (App ID F1762) to create two new systems for each communication scenario.

2.b) Use App "Communication Arrangements" (App ID F1763) to create two respective arrangements.

Note that a new service "Start Jobs to pull Plan Data from SAC" (API_FINPLANPULLJOB) has been included in the communication scenario SAP_COM_0087, that will be used in our integration task.

Note that a generic service "External Scheduler Integration" of comm. scenario SAP_COM_0326 (BC_EXT_APPJOB_MANAGEMENT) service will not be used in our integration task.

After the described configuration is done, your communication user must show up as used in the following communication artifacts:

Once communication arrangements get successfully activated, your communication user acquires all necessary authorizations to complete the desired task. The key authorizations are permission to run service API_FINPLANPULLJOB (inherited from communication scenario SAP_COM _0087) and permission to start application jobs on behalf of another user (inherited from communication scenario SAP_COM _0326).

3) Create a new business role using App “Maintain Business Roles” (App ID F1492). The minimal set of IAM Applications for performing our task include:

IAM App IDPurpose
SAC_INT_PULL_TRANFor running application "Manage Financial Plan Data Jobs for SAP Analytics Cloud Integration"
F7902_TRANFor running application "Schedule Financial Plan Data Jobs for SAP Analytics Cloud Integration"
F1240_TRAN and SP01_SIMPLE_TRAN To display results of Application Jobs, i.e. application log which was created by another (communication) user

Click on "Maintain Restrictions". Maintain restrictions for restriction type "Activities on Other User’s Jobs" so that application logs for Job Catalog Entry SAP_FINS_INT_SAC_S4 can be viewed only. Specify App Job Part = JOB, SPOOL.

Click "Back" to get back to the main page of the role editor and save.

4) You need a "monitoring" user to view application jobs and application logs. If necessary, create a new business user for this purpose using App "Maintain Business Users" (App ID F1303). Alternatively, you might already have an existing business user in the system. In any of these cases, assign your newly created business role from p. 3 to your "monitoring" user.

5) Specify the "posting" user. You can do this by assigning such user to a Business User Group with pre-defined name ZCB_SAC_PULL using App "Maintain Business User Groups" (App ID F6399).
Note that the "posting" user for starting jobs can be the same as "monitoring" user from p. 4 or they can be different S/4HANA users.

Settings in SAP Analytics Cloud

1) Create a new connection of type HTTP API:

In the next dialog specify Data Service URL in the form:
https://<<s/4hana_tenant>>:443/sap/opu/odata4/sap/api_finplanpulljob/srvd_a2x/sap/finplansacpulljob/0001/FinPlanPullJob
Authentication Type = Basic Authentication
User Name = <<communication user name (alias)>>
Password = <<password for communication user>>

2) Go to Multi Actions -> create Multi Action:

Add API Step to your Multi Action:

In the properties of API Step:

  • select HTTP API Connection from p. 1:

  • Enter API URL in the form:

https://<<s/4hana_tenant>>/sap/opu/odata4/sap/api_finplanpulljob/srvd_a2x/sap/finplansacpulljob/0001/FinPlanPullJob/SAP__self.ScheduleJob

  • Set tick mark "Require CSRF Token" on.
  • Enter CSRF Token URL in the form:

https://<<s/4hana_tenant>>:443/sap/opu/odata4/sap/api_finplanpulljob/srvd_a2x/sap/finplansacpulljob/0001/FinPlanPullJob

  • Enter Body of API request. Note that some of the parameters are optional. Refer to two examples below:
Minimal formExtended form

{
    "PlanDataImportConfigurationID": "<<your_config_ID>>"
}

{
    "PlanDataImportConfigurationID": "<<your_config_ID>>",
    "PlanDataImportIsTestMode": true/false,
    "PlanDataImportJobDelay": <<number_of_seconds>>,
    "PlanDataImportNumberOfAttempts": <<number>>
}

If job delay parameter equals to 0 or omitted, the job starts immediately. However, if you are using SAC subscriptions in your configuration, and amount of changed data in your model is big enough, then calculation of delta may take some time on SAC side. If this is the case, your job, if started immediately, may issue a request to your SAC model too early (i.e. before delta is ready on SAC side) and corresponding response may return an old state of delta (i.e. may not return some latest changes). With this parameter you can mitigate this problem by starting your job with some delay.
The “number of attempts” parameter is another way to mitigate the risk of long delta calculation. The service keeps sending requests to SAC model repeatedly several times until response returns any record. Once request returns any data, the service stops making attempts.

  • Under Generic API settings -> Response, choose option "Get API trigger status from HTTP status code and response body".
  • Press "Configure fields mapping" to map the fields of the service API_FINPLANPULLJOB with the fields of the API step:

  • In the Fields Mapping popup, go through three configuration steps:
    • For "1. Enter JSON", copy and paste the following template of response for our service:

{
"PlanDataImportJobIdentifier": "JobID",
"PlanDataImportJobMessageText": "In Process",
"PlanDataImportJobStatusText": "IN_PROCESS"
}

  • For "2. Map Fields", map three fields between response of our service and expected fields of API Step – Job ID, Status and Message:

PlanDataImportJobIdentifier = JobID
PlanDataImportStatusText = Status
PlanDataImportJobMessageText = Message

The result of the mapping must look like below:

  • For "3. Map Status Value", map three values of expected by API Step “Status” field and actual response value of our service:

  • Under Get API Execution Request, choose method “Asynchronous Return”.
  • Enter “Polling API URL” in the form:

https://<<s/4hana_tenant>>:443/sap/opu/odata4/sap/api_finplanpulljob/srvd_a2x/sap/finplansacpulljob/0001/FinPlanPullJob/SAP__self.GetJobStatus(PlanDataImportJobIdentifier='${jobId}')

  • Under Get API Execution Result -> Response, choose option "Get API execution result from HTTP status code and response body".
  • Press "Configure fields mapping" to map the fields of the service response with expected fields of the API step:

  • In the Fields Mapping popup, go through three configuration steps:
    • For “1. Enter JSON”, copy and paste the following template of response for our service:

{
"PlanDataImportJobMessageText": "Job Completed with 100 records",
"PlanDataImportJobStatusText": "DONE"
}

  • For "2. Map Fields", map two fields between response of our service and expected fields of API Step – Status and Message:
    PlanDataImportJobStatusText = Status
    PlanDataImportJobMessageText = Message

The result of the mapping must look like below:

  • For "3. Map Status Value", map three values of expected by API Step “Status” field and actual response value of our service:

Note: there is a documentation and tutorial for adding an API Step 

3) Incorporate your Multi Action into your SAC Story:

Open SAC Story and choose Insert -> Starters -> Multi Action Starter:

Specify Label, Description and select your Multi Action from p. 2:

4) Save your Story and switch to View mode.

Smoke test

1) Create your Configuration ID using App “Manage Financial Plan Data Jobs - for SAP Analytics Cloud Integration” (App ID SAC_INT_PULL). Here is an example of configuration we used in this smoke test:

2) Optionally, check that integration works as expected if you trigger it directly from the App “Schedule Financial Plan Data Jobs for SAP Analytics Cloud Integration” (App ID F7902).

3) As far as our configuration has Delta mode, in this smoke test we are going to change a data slice which is given in the filter settings of your Configuration ID. After you've saved your configuration, a new subscription gets automatically created on SAC side, which is immediately starting to monitor all the changes in the defined data slice of your model.

Go to your SAC Story and make any change(s) in the cell(s) inside this data slice.

4) Once you’ve made your changes in your SAC Story, click on Publish Data and Press Multi Action Starter.

During execution of integration job, you should see a pop-up message on the screen:

Once job is finished, you may get different messages.
In case of successful integration:

In case of an error at integration, the error message gets propagated directly to the message toast:

An error can be also caused by wrong configuration in S/4HANA or by providing incorrect parameters in the Multi Action:

Note that all messages you get in the form of message toasts are also available in the Job Monitor view:

In addition to high-level messaging in SAC Job monitor, the planner has also possibility for more deep analysis of integration flow. It may be necessary, for instance, for analysis of issues/errors. Planner may use the "monitoring" user in S/4HANA to log-in to SAP Fiori Launchpad and read application logs:

Conclusion

With the described approach, planner can benefit from two powerful features in SAC Pull framework which complement each other: so-called "Delta Mode" of integration and functionality to trigger integration by clicking a "Multi Action Starter" button in SAC Story. The first feature significantly shortens integration times, whereas the second one brings easiness of starting integration. This scenario is particularly useful where a planner modifies model data frequently in SAC Story and, on the other hand, there is a requirement to replicate these changes into S/4HANA on request.

Overview
What is RAP?
                         The ABAP RESTful Application Programming Model (RAP) is SAP's modern, cloud-ready framework for building transactional Fiori applications in ABAP Cloud. It replaces older approaches like BOPF and classic ABAP MVC, and is the standard for SAP S/4HANA Cloud and BTP ABAP Environment development.
 
RAP provides:
  • A structured, layered architecture from database to UI
  • Built-in OData service generation (no manual SEGW needed)
  • Framework-managed CRUD operations (Create, Read, Update, Delete)
  • Draft handling for save/resume workflows
  • Clean Core compliance — no modifications to SAP standard objects

What is the Managed Scenario?

TypeWho handles CRUD?When to use
ManagedRAP Framework automaticallyNew custom BOs — no legacy dependencies
UnmanagedDeveloper writes all logicWrapping legacy function modules / BAPIs

In the Managed scenario, the RAP framework automatically handles database INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, and SELECT operations. You only write code for custom business logic like validations, determinations, and custom actions. This makes it the fastest and cleanest way to build a new Business Object from scratch.

Step 1 — Database Table (Main Table)

What is it?

The database table is the foundation of your Business Object. It is the actual physical table in the SAP HANA database where all your application data is permanently stored. Every field you want to persist — travel ID, agency, customer, price, status — must be defined here first.

Why do we create it?

Without a database table, there is no place to store data. The entire RAP stack above it — CDS views, behavior definitions, OData services — are all abstractions built on top of this table. The table is the single source of truth for your BO's data.

Structure of a RAP-compliant database table

A RAP managed table must follow specific conventions:

@EndUserText.label : 'Products'
@AbapCatalog.enhancement.category : #NOT_EXTENSIBLE
@AbapCatalog.tableCategory : #TRANSPARENT
@AbapCatalog.deliveryClass : #A
@AbapCatalog.dataMaintenance : #RESTRICTED
define table znk_t_product {

  key client            : abap.clnt not null;
  key pro_uuid          : sysuuid_x16 not null;
  key product_id        : abap.char(10) not null;
  description           : abap.char(40);
  @Semantics.quantity.unitOfMeasure : 'znk_t_product.uom'
  qty                   : abap.quan(8,3);
  uom                   : abap.unit(3);
  @Semantics.amount.currencyCode : 'znk_t_product.currency'
  price                 : abap.curr(15,2);
  currency              : abap.cuky;
  mfg_date              : abap.datn;
  exp_date              : abap.datn;
  validdays             : abap.int4;
  plant                 : abap.char(4);
  local_created_by      : abp_creation_user;
  local_created_at      : abp_creation_tstmpl;
  local_last_changed_by : abp_locinst_lastchange_user;
  local_last_changed_at : abp_locinst_lastchange_tstmpl;
  last_changed_at       : abp_lastchange_tstmpl;

}

Important: The last_changed_at field with type abp_lastchange_tstmpl is critical for the ETag mechanism. When two users try to update the same record simultaneously, RAP compares this timestamp to detect conflicts and reject stale updates.

Step 2 — Draft Table (Why It Exists)

What is a Draft Table?

The draft table is a temporary storage table where incomplete, unsaved data is held while a user is still filling in a form. It has an identical structure to your main database table, with some additional draft-specific fields added by the framework.

By convention, draft tables are named the same as the main table with a _D suffix:

Main table   : ZNK_T_PRODUCT        ← permanent, saved data
Draft table  : ZNK_T_PRODUCT_D      ← temporary, in-progress data
 

Why do we need a Draft Table?

Imagine a user opens a "Create Product" form in a Fiori app and starts filling in the fields — Plant, UOM, MFG & Exp dates. Halfway through, their browser crashes, or they need to attend a meeting. Without draft handling, all their work is lost.

With Draft Handling:

User opens form
      │
      ▼
Data saved to DRAFT TABLE immediately (auto-save)
      │
      ├── User continues tomorrow → draft is still there ✅
      ├── User switches device → draft is still there ✅
      └── User clicks "Save" → data moves to MAIN TABLE ✅
                               draft record is deleted ✅
 

The draft table ensures no data loss during long-running create/edit operations. It also enables the "Edit" button behavior in Fiori apps — when you click Edit on a saved record, RAP copies the record to the draft table so your edits don't affect the live data until you explicitly save.

How to define the Draft Table

You don't write the draft table manually field by field. You reference it in your Behavior Definition and let ADT generate it:

-- In your Behavior Definition:
managed implementation in class zbp_nk_product_i unique;
strict ( 2 );
with draft;
define behavior for znk_product_I //alias <alias_name>
persistent table znk_t_product               -- ← your main table
draft table znk_t_product_d                  -- ← your draft table (RAP manages this)            
...
 

When you activate the behavior definition, ADT automatically creates the draft table with the correct structure.

     Step 3 — Interface View (Z*_I)

What is the Interface View?

The Interface View is the base CDS View Entity that sits directly on top of your database table. It forms the service-agnostic data model of your Business Object — meaning it defines the complete data structure without any UI-specific concerns.

By convention, Interface Views are prefixed with ZR_ (R = Root) for root entities or ZI_ (I = Interface).

    entity.name: 'I_Currency',

Why do we need the Interface View?

The Interface View serves several critical purposes:

1. Abstraction from the database table The database table uses technical field names and types. The Interface View can rename, cast, and join fields into a cleaner business model. If the table structure changes, only the interface view needs to be updated — everything above is unaffected.

2. It is the root of the composition tree The keyword define root view entity declares this as the top of a Business Object hierarchy. All child entities (like Booking under Travel) are connected back to this root via COMPOSITION OF associations.

3. It is reusable across multiple services The interface view has NO UI annotations, NO Fiori-specific logic. This means the same interface view can power:

  • A Fiori Elements app (via projection view → OData)
  • A remote API (via a different projection)

4. Associations are defined here Associations to related entities (Currency, UnitOfMeasure) are defined on the interface view so they are available to all Products.

The define root view entity keyword

This keyword does two important things:

  • It declares this CDS view as a Root Entity of a Business Object
  • It enables it to have its own Behavior Definition repository object
  • Only root entities can define composition of child associations
  Step 4 — Consumption View (Z*_C)

What is the Consumption View?

The Consumption View (also called the Projection View) sits on top of the Interface View and represents a service-specific, tailored window into the Business Object. It is what gets exposed to the outside world — via OData, via a Fiori app, via an API.

By convention, Consumption Views are prefixed or suffixed with ZC_ (C = Consumption).

  association [1..1] to znk_product_I as _BaseEntity on $projection.ProUuid = _BaseEntity.ProUuid
                                                    and $projection.ProductId = _BaseEntity.ProductId
{
key ProUuid,
key ProductId,
Description,
@Semantics.quantity.unitOfMeasure: 'Uom'
Qty,
@Consumption.valueHelpDefinition:[{ entity:{ name: 'I_UnitOfMeasure',
                                             element: 'UnitOfMeasure'},
                                    useForValidation: true }]
Uom,
@Semantics.amount.currencyCode: 'Currency'
Price,
@Consumption.valueHelpDefinition: [{ entity:{ name: 'I_Currency',
                                     element: 'Currency' },
                                     useForValidation: true  }]
Currency,
MfgDate,
ExpDate,
Plant,
ValidDays,
LocalCreatedBy,
LocalCreatedAt,
LocalLastChangedBy,
LocalLastChangedAt,
LastChangedAt,

Why do we need the Consumption View if we already have the Interface View?

This is the most common question from beginners. The answer is separation of concerns:

 
Concern Interface View✅Consumption View
Business data model✅Defined hereInherited from interface
Associations & compositions✅Defined hereRedirected here
UI annotations (@UI.*)❌Not here✅Via Metadata Extension
Value helps (@Consumption.valueHelpDefinition)❌Not here✅Defined here
Field aliasing for UI❌Not here✅Can rename fields
Access control✅Defined hereAdditional checks possible
Which fields to exposeAll fieldsSubset — only what the app needs

Real-world analogy:             

                       Think of the Interface View as a master employee record with every piece of data. The Consumption View is a role-specific form an HR manager sees salary and personal data, a project manager sees only skills and availability. Same underlying data, different projections.

The as projection on syntax

This is what makes a view a projection view. It tells the RAP framework:

  • "This view is consuming/projecting another view"
  • "The underlying BO's behavior definition applies through here"
  • "Compositions must be redirected to their own projection equivalents"

Why do we use a Metadata Extension instead of putting annotations directly in the CDS view?

There are three powerful reasons:

1. Clean Separation of Concerns The CDS view defines WHAT data exists. The Metadata Extension defines HOW it looks in the UI. Mixing both in one file creates a massive, hard-to-read view definition. Separating them keeps each file focused and maintainable.

2. Extensibility (Key User / Partner / Customer layers) The @Metadata.layer annotation supports a hierarchy:

#CORE          ← SAP / developer defines base UI
#CUSTOMER      ← Customer adds their annotations
#PARTNER       ← Relates to a partner extension of a product 
#INDUSTRY      ← Relates to an industry-specific extension of a product (SAP Industry Solution)
 

Lower layers can be overridden by higher layers without modifying the original files. This is the foundation of SAP's extensibility model.

3. Keeps the CDS View Clean for Multiple Consumers If you put @UI.lineItem directly in the CDS view, those annotations are baked in for everyone. With a metadata extension, different services can have different metadata extensions on the same projection view — different UI layouts for different apps.

⚙️Step 6 — Behavior Definition (Interface View)

What is a Behavior Definition?

A Behavior Definition (BDEF) is a repository object that defines what operations are allowed on a Business Object. It answers questions like:

  • Can this BO be created, updated, deleted?
  • Which fields are read-only or mandatory?
  • Does it support draft handling?
  • What custom actions exist (like "Valid Days")?
  • How are primary keys generated?

Interface View Behavior Definition

The base BDEF sits on the Interface View and defines the complete set of capabilities of the BO:

managed implementation in class zbp_nk_product_i unique;
strict ( 2 );
with draft;
define behavior for znk_product_I //alias <alias_name>
persistent table znk_t_product
draft table znk_t_product_d
lock master                                                         -- Locking mechanism
total etag LastChangedAt
authorization master ( global )
etag master LastChangedAt                                           -- ETag for concurrency control
{

 -- Field controls
 field ( mandatory : create ) ProductId;                            -- Makes Mandatory when create
 field ( readonly )                                                 -- Makes non-editable
 LocalCreatedAt,
 LocalCreatedBy,
 LocalLastChangedAt,
 LocalLastChangedBy,
 LastChangedAt;
 field ( numbering : managed ) ProUuid;                             -- Makes Numbering Managed
 field ( readonly : update ) ProUuid, ProductId;                    -- Makes non-editable when update

   -- Standard CRUD operations (framework handles automatically in managed)
  create;
  update;
  delete;

  -- Custom actions (developer implements)
  action  ( features : instance ) checkProductValidity result [1] $self;
  action  ( features : instance ) clearValidDays result [1] $self;

  -- Draft related Actions
  draft action Edit;
  draft action Activate optimized;
  draft action Discard;
  draft action Resume;
  draft determine action Prepare;

  -- Mapping is very important to store the values to DB 
  mapping for znk_t_product
    {
      ProUuid            = pro_uuid;
      ProductId          = product_id;
      Description        = description;
      Qty                = qty;
      Uom                = uom;
      Price              = price;
      Currency           = currency;
      MfgDate            = mfg_date;
      ExpDate            = exp_date;
      Plant              = plant;
      ValidDays          = validdays;
      LocalCreatedBy     = local_created_by;
      LocalCreatedAt     = local_created_at;
      LocalLastChangedAt = local_last_changed_at;
      LocalLastChangedBy = local_last_changed_by;
      LastChangedAt      = last_changed_at;
    }
}
 

Key BDEF keywords explained

managed — Tells the RAP framework to auto-handle all database operations (INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE). You don't write any MODIFY dbtab statements yourself.

with draft — Activates the draft handling mechanism. The framework will use your draft table for all in-progress changes.

etag master LocalLastChangedAt — Enables optimistic locking. Before any update, RAP compares the LocalLastChangedAt timestamp in the request with the database to detect if someone else modified the record in between.

lock master — When a user starts editing (enters draft mode), the record is locked so no other user can simultaneously edit the same record.

numbering:managed — (when used on a field) Tells the framework to auto-generate a UUID primary key at CREATE time — no manual key assignment needed.

validation — A method you implement in the Behavior Implementation class. Called by the framework before save. Return error messages to block the save.

determination — A method that auto-runs when specific fields change. Used for defaulting values (e.g., set status to "Open" when a Product is created).

action — A custom operation beyond standard CRUD. Adds a button in the Fiori UI. Example: "Valid Days" changes status to Accepted.

🔒Step 7 — Behavior Definition (Projection View)

What is the Projection Behavior Definition?

The Projection BDEF sits on the Consumption View and exposes a subset of the base BDEF's operations for a specific service. It acts as a gatekeeper — you decide which operations this particular OData service gets to offer.

projection;
strict ( 2 );
use draft;

define behavior for znk_product_c //alias <alias_name>
{
  use create;                           -- Expose create to this service
  use update;                           -- Expose update to this service
  use delete;                           -- Expose delete to this service

  use action Edit;
  use action Activate;
  use action Discard;
  use action Prepare;
  use action Resume;


  -- Expose only the custom actions this service needs
  use action checkProductValidity;
  use action clearValidDays;
}

💻Step 8 — Behavior Implementation (BAP)

What is the Behavior Implementation?

The Behavior Implementation is an ABAP class that contains the actual code for all custom operations defined in the base Behavior Definition — validations, determinations, and actions. In managed scenarios, you do NOT write code for standard CRUD — the framework handles that. You only write code for your custom business logic.

The class is named in the BDEF with implementation in class zbp_nk_product_i unique;.

ENDCLASS.

CLASS zbp_nk_product_i IMPLEMENTATION.
ENDCLASS.
 

The actual logic sits in local classes inside the implementation class's .locals_imp include:

Validation Example — validateDates

CLASS lhc_znk_product_I DEFINITION INHERITING FROM cl_abap_behavior_handler.
  PRIVATE SECTION.
    METHODS get_global_authorizations FOR GLOBAL AUTHORIZATION
    REQUEST requested_authorizations FOR znk_product_I RESULT result.
    METHODS checkProductValidity FOR MODIFY
       keys FOR ACTION znk_product_I~checkProductValidity RESULT result.
    METHODS get_instance_features FOR INSTANCE FEATURES
      keys REQUEST requested_features FOR znk_product_I RESULT result.
    METHODS clearvaliddays FOR MODIFY
       keys FOR ACTION znk_product_i~clearvaliddays RESULT result.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS lhc_znk_product_I IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD get_global_authorizations.
  ENDMETHOD.

  METHOD checkProductValidity.

    READ ENTITIES OF znk_product_I IN LOCAL MODE                               --Read entries from Interface view to lt_products
        ENTITY znk_product_I
        FIELDS ( MfgDate ExpDate )
        WITH CORRESPONDING #( keys )
        RESULT DATA(lt_products)
        FAILED DATA(ls_failed).

    MODIFY ENTITIES OF znk_product_I IN LOCAL MODE                             --Modify entries from Interface view to lt_products
        ENTITY znk_product_I
        UPDATE FIELDS ( ValidDays )
        WITH VALUE #(
          FOR ls IN lt_products
          LET lv_days = CONV i( ls-ExpDate - ls-MfgDate )
          IN ( %tky      = ls-%tky
               ValidDays = lv_days ) ).

    LOOP AT lt_products INTO DATA(ls_product).                                  --Validation on to lt_products
      IF ls_product-ExpDate <= ls_product-MfgDate.
        APPEND VALUE #(
          %tky = ls_product-%tky
          %msg = new_message_with_text(
                   severity = if_abap_behv_message=>severity-error
                   text     = 'Expiry Date must be after Manufacturing Date!' )
        ) TO reported-znk_product_i.
      ENDIF.
    ENDLOOP.
    READ ENTITIES OF znk_product_I IN LOCAL MODE
                                   ENTITY znk_product_I
                                   ALL FIELDS
                                   WITH CORRESPONDING #( keys )
                                   RESULT DATA(lt_result).

    result = VALUE #( FOR ls IN lt_result                                        --Return the modified entries to result
                      ( %tky   = ls-%tky
                        %param = ls ) ).   

  ENDMETHOD.

  METHOD get_instance_features.
    READ ENTITIES OF znk_product_I IN LOCAL MODE
     ENTITY znk_product_I
     FIELDS ( ProductId )
     WITH CORRESPONDING #( keys )
     RESULT DATA(lt_products)
     FAILED DATA(ls_failed).

    result = VALUE #( FOR ls IN lt_products
                      ( %tky                          = ls-%tky
                        %action-checkProductValidity  = if_abap_behv=>fc-o-enabled ) ).
  ENDMETHOD.

  METHOD clearValidDays.
    READ ENTITIES OF znk_product_I IN LOCAL MODE
        ENTITY znk_product_I
        FIELDS ( MfgDate ExpDate )
        WITH CORRESPONDING #( keys )
        RESULT DATA(lt_products)
        FAILED DATA(ls_failed).

    MODIFY ENTITIES OF znk_product_I IN LOCAL MODE
        ENTITY znk_product_I
        UPDATE FIELDS ( ValidDays )
        WITH VALUE #(
          FOR ls IN lt_products
          LET lv_days = 0
          IN ( %tky      = ls-%tky
               ValidDays = lv_days ) ).

    READ ENTITIES OF znk_product_I IN LOCAL MODE
                      ENTITY znk_product_I
                      ALL FIELDS
                      WITH CORRESPONDING #( keys )
                      RESULT DATA(lt_result).
    result = VALUE #( FOR ls IN lt_result
        ( %tky   = ls-%tky
          %param = ls ) ).   
  ENDMETHOD.

ENDCLASS.
 

Determination Example — setInitialStatus

METHOD setInitialStatus.
  " Read travels that were just created
  READ ENTITIES OF zr_traveltp IN LOCAL MODE
    ENTITY Travel
      FIELDS ( OverallStatus )
      WITH CORRESPONDING #( keys )
    RESULT DATA(lt_travel)
    FAILED failed.

  " Filter: only set status if it's initial (empty)
  DELETE lt_travel WHERE OverallStatus IS NOT INITIAL.
  CHECK lt_travel IS NOT INITIAL.

  " Set default status to 'Open'
  MODIFY ENTITIES OF zr_traveltp IN LOCAL MODE
    ENTITY Travel
      UPDATE FIELDS ( OverallStatus )
      WITH VALUE #( FOR ls_travel IN lt_travel (
        %tky          = ls_travel-%tky
        OverallStatus = 'O'   " O = Open
      ) )
    REPORTED DATA(lt_reported).

  reported = CORRESPONDING #( DEEP lt_reported ).
ENDMETHOD.
 

Action Example — checkProductValidity

METHOD checkProductValidity.

    READ ENTITIES OF znk_product_I IN LOCAL MODE
        ENTITY znk_product_I
        FIELDS ( MfgDate ExpDate )
        WITH CORRESPONDING #( keys )
        RESULT DATA(lt_products)
        FAILED DATA(ls_failed).

    MODIFY ENTITIES OF znk_product_I IN LOCAL MODE
        ENTITY znk_product_I
        UPDATE FIELDS ( ValidDays )
        WITH VALUE #(
          FOR ls IN lt_products
          LET lv_days = CONV i( ls-ExpDate - ls-MfgDate )
          IN ( %tky      = ls-%tky
               ValidDays = lv_days ) ).

    LOOP AT lt_products INTO DATA(ls_product).
      IF ls_product-ExpDate <= ls_product-MfgDate.
        APPEND VALUE #(
          %tky = ls_product-%tky
          %msg = new_message_with_text(
                   severity = if_abap_behv_message=>severity-error
                   text     = 'Expiry Date must be after Manufacturing Date!' )
        ) TO reported-znk_product_i.
      ENDIF.
    ENDLOOP.
    READ ENTITIES OF znk_product_I IN LOCAL MODE
                                   ENTITY znk_product_I
                                   ALL FIELDS
                                   WITH CORRESPONDING #( keys )
                                   RESULT DATA(lt_result).

    result = VALUE #( FOR ls IN lt_result
                      ( %tky   = ls-%tky
                        %param = ls ) ).   

  ENDMETHOD.
 

Important RAP-specific ABAP concepts

READ ENTITIES — The RAP-specific way to read data from a BO. Always use this inside behavior implementations — never use SELECT directly.

MODIFY ENTITIES — The RAP-specific way to change data inside behavior implementations — never use MODIFY dbtab directly.

IN LOCAL MODE — Bypasses authorization checks and feature controls when called from within the same BO's implementation. Important for internal BO operations.

%tky — The transactional key — a structure containing all key fields of the entity. Used to identify records throughout RAP's internal processing.

failed / reported — Standard output parameters for all RAP methods. Populate failed to signal which records errored. Populate reported to send messages back to the UI.

🌐Step 9 — Service Definition & Service Binding

Service Definition

Defines which CDS entities are exposed and under what names:

@EndUserText.label: 'Service Definition for Consumption view'
define service Znk_sd_product {
  expose znk_product_c;
}
 

Service Binding

The Service Binding ties a Service Definition to a specific protocol and usage type. For Fiori apps, you create an OData V4 binding with type UI:

  • Binding Type: OData V4 - UI
  • Activate the binding to get the OData service URL
  • Use "Preview" in ADT to open the Fiori Elements app directly

Once activated, your Product BO is fully functional as a Fiori Elements List Report + Object Page app — with list, filter, create, edit, draft, save, and all your custom actions.

💡Key Takeaways

The Purpose of Each Layer — Summary

DATABASE TABLE     → Where data lives permanently
DRAFT TABLE        → Where in-progress data lives temporarily
INTERFACE VIEW     → Clean data model, service-agnostic, reusable
CONSUMPTION VIEW   → Service-specific window — what this app sees
METADATA EXTENSION → UI layout — how fields look in Fiori
BASE BDEF          → All possible BO operations defined
PROJECTION BDEF    → Subset of operations for this specific service
BAP CLASS          → Custom business logic — validations, actions
SERVICE DEFINITION → Which entities go into the OData service
SERVICE BINDING    → Which protocol (OData V4) and port (UI/API)
 

The Two-Layer Pattern (Interface + Consumption) — Why it matters

The separation of Interface and Consumption layers is the most important design decision in RAP. It gives you:

  1. Reusability — one BO, multiple services (UI service, API service, integration service)
  2. Flexibility — each service exposes exactly what it needs
  3. Stability — changing the UI doesn't break the underlying BO contract
  4. Extensibility — SAP's own S/4HANA BOs follow this same pattern

Managed vs Unmanaged at a glance

In this managed scenario, the RAP framework wrote all the database interaction code for you. You only wrote:

  • Validation logic (validateDates)
  • Determination logic (setInitialStatus)
  • Action logic (checkProductValidity, Clear)

Everything else — INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, draft handling, locking, ETag — was handled by the framework automatically.

Github Link :  RAP-Managed-in-SAP 

Thanks,

Naveen Kumar SAP ABAP Developer | BTP Explorer

entry.title: Why Recorded SAP GUI Scripts Are Hard to Maintain (and What to Do About It)
entry.content:
Disclosure: I work on a test automation tool for SAP GUI. The problems below are ones we ran into while building it, but everything in this post applies to plain SAP GUI Scripting with VBScript or any other language.

The SAP GUI Script Recorder is one of the fastest ways to automate a transaction. You press record, run through VA01 once, and you get a working script in a few minutes.

Then the script breaks after a support package, fails on a colleague's PC, or reports success for an order that was never created. The trouble isn't the recorder. A recording captures one run of the transaction on one screen setup, and a test needs to work for many runs. Here are the most common reasons recorded scripts become hard to maintain, and some general ways to deal with each one.

1. Control IDs are absolute paths into the screen layout

A typical recorded line looks like this:

session.findById("wnd[0]/usr/subSUBSCREEN_HEADER:SAPMV45A:4021/subPART-SUB:SAPMV45A:4701/ctxtKUAGV-KUNNR").text = "1000"

The ID contains every container on the way to the field, including subscreen program names and screen numbers. Those depend on things that change over time:

  • Customizing that changes which subscreen is shown (order type, sales area, and so on)
  • Support packages or enhancements that rearrange screens
  • Tab strips, where the same field sits under a different path depending on the active tab

When any part of the path changes, findById fails, even though the field itself (KUAGV-KUNNR) is still on the screen.

What helps: search for the field by its technical name inside a stable container instead of hard-coding the full path.

Set usr = session.findById("wnd[0]/usr")
Set fld = usr.FindByName("KUAGV-KUNNR", "GuiCTextField")
fld.text = soldTo

FindByName searches the container's children, so the script no longer cares which subscreen the field ended up in. If the same name appears more than once, use FindAllByName and choose the one you need on purpose.

2. Test data is baked into the script

The recorder writes every value you typed straight into the code: order type, customer, material, quantity. To test a second customer, people copy the script and edit the values. After a few months there are twenty almost identical scripts, and a single screen change means twenty edits.

What helps: keep the transaction logic in one place and read the data from outside (a CSV file, a spreadsheet, or a parameter list). One script plus one data table is much easier to maintain than twenty copies.

3. Only the happy path is recorded

During recording, the transaction followed one path. In real runs, SAP shows extra windows depending on the data and the situation:

  • An information popup about credit limits or incompletion
  • A "Data will be lost" confirmation
  • A warning message in the status bar that needs another Enter

The recorded script doesn't know these exist. When a popup appears, the next findById on wnd[0] fails because the active window is now wnd[1].

What helps: after each step that can trigger a popup, check whether a modal window is open and handle it explicitly.

Function HandlePopupIfAny(session)
    Dim popup
    Set popup = session.findById("wnd[1]", False)   ' returns Nothing instead of raising
    If Not popup Is Nothing Then
        LogInfo "Popup: " & popup.Text
        popup.sendVKey 0                             ' or a specific button, based on the title
    End If
End Function

Decide case by case which popups are expected and which should fail the test. Pressing Enter on every popup silently can hide real problems.

4. Table rows are addressed by visible position

Recorded table access looks like this:

session.findById(".../tblSAPMV45ATCTRL_U_ERF_AUFTRAG/ctxtRV45A-MABNR[1,0]").text = "MAT-001"

In a GuiTableControl, the row index refers to the visible area, not the absolute row. How many rows are visible depends on the window size and screen resolution. A script that fills row 12 works on a large monitor and fails on a laptop. In ALV grids (GuiGridView), row positions also change when the user's layout sorts or filters the data.

What helps:

  • For table controls, scroll with VerticalScrollbar.Position and calculate the visible index from the absolute row.
  • For ALV grids, find the row by its content (for example, loop over RowCount and compare GetCellValue) instead of assuming a fixed position.
  • Don't depend on the maximized window size you happened to have during recording.

5. The recorder records actions, not checks

A recorded script ends right after the last click. If the order wasn't saved because of an error message, the script still finishes without errors. From the script's point of view, everything "worked".

What helps: add an explicit check after each important step. The status bar is the simplest place to start.

Set sbar = session.findById("wnd[0]/sbar")
If sbar.MessageType = "E" Or sbar.MessageType = "A" Then
    Fail "Save failed: " & sbar.Text
End If
orderNo = ExtractNumber(sbar.Text)   ' keep the result for later steps or reports

A test without checks can only tell you that the screens didn't crash. It can't tell you that the business process worked.

6. The environment leaks into the script

Some failures come from the user or the PC, not from the script:

  • User parameters (SU3): default values such as sales organization or plant are filled in automatically for one user and left empty for another.
  • Logon language: scripts that select dropdown entries or buttons by text break in another language. Use keys instead of texts where possible.
  • Personalization: saved ALV layouts, hidden columns, or screen variants change what is on the screen.

What helps: set every field the test depends on explicitly, even when it is usually prefilled, and use technical keys rather than display texts.

7. When a script fails, the error tells you almost nothing

A typical failure message is "The control could not be found by id" plus a line number. To understand what happened, someone has to run the script again and watch the screen.

What helps: log every step with the transaction code, the screen (session.Info.Program and session.Info.ScreenNumber), and the status bar text, and take a screenshot (HardCopy) when a step fails. The person who fixes the script is often not the person who wrote it, so this context saves a lot of time.

8. Everything is one long script

Recordings produce one long sequence: logon, navigation, data entry, and save, all in one file. Logon and navigation are then copied into every script. When the logon screen or a common menu path changes, every copy needs to be updated.

What helps: split the script into reusable building blocks, such as "start transaction", "fill header", "add item", "save and check", and "handle popup". Then build each test from those blocks.

Summary

A recording is a good starting point, but it isn't a test yet. Before you put a recorded script into regular use, check the following:

  1. Are fields found by name inside stable containers instead of by long absolute paths?
  2. Is the test data kept outside the script?
  3. Are possible popups and warnings handled on purpose?
  4. Are table rows found by content, independent of window size?
  5. Does every important step have a check?
  6. Is every required field set explicitly, using keys instead of texts?
  7. Does a failure leave enough context (screen, message, screenshot) to diagnose it?
  8. Are common steps shared instead of copied?

We ran into all of these while building PerfecTwin ERP, a test automation tool for SAP GUI, and most of them took longer to solve than we expected. I'd like to hear how others deal with them, especially popup handling and ALV grids. Please share your approach in the comments.

entry.title: Finance in SAP Cloud ERP 2608
entry.content:
Hello finance experts! I’m excited to walk you through the latest finance innovations introduced in our 2608 release.
 
This update is loaded with capabilities that add more intelligence, automation, and visibility to your finance operations. We’re continuing our mission to streamline core activities, elevate analytical depth, and enable quicker, data-driven decisions.
 
Want the short version of the top Finance highlights in 2608? Watch my quick video.
 
For a complete rundown of everything included in this release, take a look at the table of contents below.
 
Let’s jump into the highlights!
 
Video 1. Release Highlight Video for Finance in SAP Cloud ERP 2608

Table of Content

This update highlights significant innovations in the following areas:

Accounting & Financial Close

  • End-to-end cost settlement process (CLM)
  • Introduction of configurable depreciation profiles
  • SAP Fiori app for posting asset transfers
  • Central Task Model management
  • Journal Entry Agent

Financial Planning & Analysis​

  • Comprehensive analytical capabilities for material values in actual costing
  • AI-assisted error resolution for cost accounting

Treasury & Working Capital

  • Receivables and Payables Clearing Agent (Demo video) 
  • Payment Inquiry Handling Agent
  • Risk-based payment approvals 
  • Bank Statement Processing
  • Dynamic discounting
  • Enrichment of Bank Statement Items
  • Enhancements to Matching Algorithms
  • Editable email body in Create Correspondence app

Revenue Management 

  • Enabling Custom Fields for the Contract Account RAP Object
  • Managing Direct Debit Prenotifications in Contract Accounting
  • Display of General Ledger Items in Contract Accounting (Demo video)

Accounting & Financial Close

End-to-end cost settlement process (CLM)
The latest 2608 release of SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition introduces a range of powerful capabilities, including the new End-to-end cost settlement process within the Finance capability area. While the provided reference document lists this as a key innovation, it does not contain a detailed description of its specific functionalities. However, based on standard SAP principles and the direction of financial innovations, we can explore what such a process entails and the value it delivers to your organization.

An end-to-end cost settlement process is a critical function for maintaining financial accuracy and transparency. In essence, it governs the complete lifecycle of how costs are collected and allocated throughout the organization. This process involves capturing costs from various sources such as internal orders, projects, or cost centers where expenses are initially incurred and systematically settling them to their final destination cost objects, like a fixed asset, a profitability segment, or another department. A robust, integrated process ensures that all expenditures are accounted for correctly, providing a true and fair view of costs for specific activities, products, or services.

The primary benefit of implementing a comprehensive cost settlement process is the significant improvement in financial control and operational efficiency. By automating the periodic allocation of costs, businesses can drastically reduce the manual effort required during period-end closing, which in turn minimizes the risk of human error and accelerates the closing cycle. This automation leads to greater transparency, as it provides a clear and auditable trail of how costs flow through the enterprise. Ultimately, this empowers management with more accurate and timely data for crucial activities such as profitability analysis, budget monitoring, and informed strategic decision-making.

Introduction of configurable depreciation profiles

In essence, this feature provides organizations with greater control and flexibility over how they calculate and manage the depreciation of their fixed assets. Instead of being limited to standard, predefined depreciation methods, finance professionals can now define and customize their own depreciation calculation rules directly within the system to meet specific business or regulatory needs.

The primary benefit of this new capability is the enhanced flexibility it offers for global and local compliance. Many businesses operate in jurisdictions with unique statutory requirements for asset valuation that may not be covered by standard depreciation keys. Configurable depreciation profiles empower users to create tailored calculation methods that precisely align with these local accounting principles, reducing the need for manual workarounds and complex spreadsheets outside the ERP system. Consequently, this leads to more accurate and compliant financial reporting, improves the efficiency of period-end closing activities, and ensures that asset values are reflected correctly on the balance sheet, thereby strengthening financial governance and transparency across the enterprise.

SAP Fiori app for posting asset transfers

As part of our commitment to enhancing core financial processes, SAP has introduced a new SAP Fiori app specifically for posting asset transfers. This application provides a modern, user-friendly interface dedicated to managing the movement of fixed assets within your organization. In simple terms, this tool is designed to streamline the process of executing various transfer scenarios, such as moving an asset from one company code to another or reclassifying an asset. By leveraging the intuitive SAP Fiori user experience, this app simplifies a critical function within asset accounting.

The introduction of this dedicated Fiori application delivers significant benefits to finance professionals. The primary advantage is a marked improvement in user efficiency and process transparency. The app offers a guided, intuitive workflow that reduces the manual effort and complexity traditionally associated with asset transfers. This simplification helps minimize the risk of data entry errors and accelerates tasks related to asset portfolio management. Consequently, organizations can achieve a more agile and controlled approach to asset accounting, ensuring that asset data remains accurate and compliant across the enterprise.

Central Task Model management

This new feature provides a unified and simplified approach to managing your financial closing tasks. Essentially, Central Task Model management allows users to create, edit, publish, and delete task models directly within the SAP Advanced Financial Closing interface. Previously, this process required switching to a separate communication system. Now, the entire lifecycle of task models, including the maintenance of task model types and job variants, is consolidated into a single, intuitive environment. Once a task model is published, it becomes immediately available for use in your task list templates, facilitating the swift creation and reuse of standardized closing activities.

The primary benefit of this centralized approach is a marked increase in operational efficiency for both IT and business users. By eliminating the need to navigate between different systems, we significantly reduce the manual effort and time required to manage closing tasks. This streamlined workflow allows for the faster creation and deployment of reusable task definitions, making your financial close process more agile and responsive. Furthermore, the feature introduces a dedicated change log, which offers complete transparency and auditability by tracking all modifications made to task models and their related objects. This enhances governance and control, ensuring your financial closing activities are both efficient and compliant.

Journal Entry Agent

The Journal Entry Agent is a powerful new tool designed to fundamentally automate and simplify the creation of journal entries within SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition. In essence, it acts as an intelligent assistant that processes spreadsheet data to generate accurate and compliant financial postings. Users can initiate this process conversationally by submitting data files through our digital assistant, Joule. The agent then analyzes the spreadsheet's content, automatically maps the columns to the required journal entry fields, and produces structured proposals. These proposals are then made available for finance professionals to review, adjust if necessary, and post via the dedicated Manage Journal Entry Proposals application.

Image 01. Journal Entry Agent

The primary benefit of utilizing the Journal Entry Agent is a significant increase in operational efficiency and accuracy. By automating what is often a time-consuming and manual task, the agent drastically reduces the time spent on data entry, allowing your finance team to focus on more strategic, value-added activities. This automation also improves the accuracy of journal entries, minimizing the risk of errors. Furthermore, the feature enhances transparency, as each generated proposal is directly linked to its source file, ensuring a clear and auditable trail. Ultimately, these capabilities streamline the entire journal entry workflow, contributing to a faster and more efficient period-end closing process for your organization.

Financial Planning & Analysis

Comprehensive analytical capabilities for material values in actual costing

The recent 2608 release of SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition introduces a significant advancement within the Finance portfolio: Comprehensive analytical capabilities for material values in actual costing. In simple terms, actual costing is a method used to determine the true cost of materials after a period has ended by incorporating variances, such as those from purchase prices or resource consumption. While this provides a highly accurate financial picture, analyzing the vast amount of resulting data can be complex. This new feature directly addresses that challenge by providing powerful, embedded tools to dissect and understand the detailed components of your material costs with greater ease and clarity.

Video 2.Comprehensive analytical capabilities for material values in actual costing

The primary benefit of this enhancement is the profound level of transparency it offers to financial controllers and cost accountants. By leveraging these new analytical capabilities, users can move beyond high-level summaries to perform deep-dive analyses into cost drivers and variances. This facilitates more accurate profitability analysis, empowers more informed make-or-buy decisions, and helps identify opportunities for cost optimization within the supply chain. Ultimately, this leads to a more streamlined and insightful period-end closing process, reducing manual effort and enabling your finance teams to become strategic partners to the business by providing actionable intelligence derived directly from your actual material values.

AI-assisted error resolution for cost accounting

As part of the recent 2608 release for SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition, we are excited to introduce a suite of intelligent capabilities. Among these is the new AI-assisted error resolution for cost accounting. This feature is designed to fundamentally simplify and accelerate how finance professionals handle discrepancies within their cost accounting processes. In essence, it leverages the power of artificial intelligence to proactively identify, analyze, and guide users in resolving errors that can occur during critical tasks like cost allocations, internal settlements, and other period-end closing activities. By intelligently diagnosing the root cause of an issue, the system can reduce the need for extensive manual investigation, empowering users to address problems more efficiently.

The primary benefit of this innovation is a significant increase in both speed and accuracy for the financial close process. Cost accountants can move away from time-consuming, manual error-hunting and instead focus on value-added analysis, guided by AI-powered suggestions. This not only accelerates the resolution of issues but also enhances the overall quality and reliability of financial data. By streamlining a traditionally complex and labor-intensive area, AI-assisted error resolution helps reduce the pressure of period-end closing, minimizes the risk of human error, and ensures that management reporting is based on more accurate and timely information. This new capability marks another step forward in our commitment to embedding intelligent automation directly into core financial processes.

Treasury & Working Capital

Receivables and Payables Clearing Agent

The Receivables and Payables Clearing Agent is an intelligent solution designed to optimize and accelerate your periodic clearing activities for both accounts payable and accounts receivable. This agent analyzes open items and generates balanced matching proposals by leveraging commonly used reference fields to intelligently pair invoices and payments. These proposals are then validated by the system before being presented to your AP/AR accountants for final review and posting, all within dedicated SAP Fiori applications.

Video 3. Receivables and Payables Clearing Agent

The primary benefit of this agent is a significant reduction in the manual effort traditionally associated with matching and clearing open items. By providing clear explanations for its matching logic and automating the proposal generation, the agent accelerates clearing cycles and minimizes the risk of human error. This enhances operational efficiency, allowing your finance professionals to manage a higher volume of transactions with greater accuracy and confidence, ultimately freeing up their time for more analytical tasks.

Payment Inquiry Handling Agent

We are excited to introduce the Payment Inquiry Handling Agent, an AI-powered assistant embedded within SAP S/4HANA Cloud and accessible via our digital assistant, SAP Joule. This agent serves as a single, conversational point of contact for resolving accounts payable payment inquiries. Your AP accountants can now use natural language to ask questions or upload files to identify invoices. The agent connects directly to live financial data to check payment eligibility, propose appropriate payment methods, and guide the user from inquiry to resolution.

This innovation drastically accelerates the resolution of urgent payment questions, reducing a process that could take hours down to mere minutes. By eliminating the need to manually navigate through various SAP transactions, the agent significantly reduces manual coordination and administrative overhead. It empowers your AP team to provide faster, more accurate responses to payment status queries, improving both internal efficiency and supplier relationships.

Risk-based payment approvals 

Balancing payment security with operational efficiency is a critical challenge for every organization. The new risk-based payment approvals feature addresses this by introducing an intelligent workflow that automatically assesses the risk level of self-initiated payments. Using configurable risk signals such as one-time accounts, deviating payment data compared to master records, and payment source tagging the system calculates a risk score and routes payments accordingly. Low-risk payments can be processed automatically, while high-risk transactions are routed for manual review.

The value of this feature is threefold. Firstly, it increases straight-through processing rates by automating approvals for safe, low-risk payments, which accelerates your payment cycles. Secondly, it strengthens your financial controls and reduces exposure to fraud or errors through systematic, automated risk assessment. Finally, it optimizes the allocation of your finance resources by focusing their valuable time and attention exclusively on the transactions that warrant manual scrutiny, creating a more efficient and secure payment environment.

Bank Statement Processing: Value Extraction for Unstructured Fields (Memo Line) 

This innovation addresses the long-standing challenge of manually interpreting valuable data, such as invoice numbers or customer details, embedded within unstructured text fields like the memo line. With this new capability, you can now systematically automate the retrieval of key information. Using the dedicated SAP Fiori app, **Manage Value Extraction Rules - For Bank Statements (F9297)**, you can define specific, pattern-based rules to scan the memo line and extract relevant data points automatically upon ingestion of the bank statement, structuring it for use before the formal reconciliation process even begins.

The primary benefit of this innovation is a substantial increase in the efficiency and automation of your bank statement processing, which directly reduces the manual effort and operational overhead associated with reconciliation. By instructing the system on precisely what to look for, the extracted information is seamlessly passed to subsequent steps to identify the correct customer or open item, dramatically accelerating the matching process. This automation frees your finance professionals from tedious, repetitive tasks, allowing them to focus on more strategic activities like resolving complex exceptions. Ultimately, this enhancement improves data quality by minimizing manual input errors, leading to a more reliable and streamlined financial close.

Dynamic discounting : Automated Credit Memo Archival

For organizations utilizing dynamic discounting, regulatory compliance and document management are paramount. This release introduces a crucial integration with SAP Taulia for automated credit memo PDF archival. In jurisdictions where a formal credit document is required to accompany a discount taken on an early payment, SAP Taulia generates a legally compliant, digitally signed credit memo PDF. This new feature ensures that this PDF is automatically archived in SAP S/4HANA Cloud and stored against the corresponding financial journal entry using SAP's Harmonized Document Management (HDM) framework.

This automation delivers significant benefits by ensuring regulatory compliance with document archival mandates, particularly across the EU and beyond. It completely eliminates the manual effort of retrieving PDFs from an external portal and reattaching them within the ERP system, saving time and preventing errors. As your dynamic discounting program grows, this fully automated solution scales effortlessly, with no additional per-transaction overhead. It ensures your financial records are complete, compliant, and easily auditable.

Enrichment of Bank Statement Items

In the complex landscape of financial operations, the new "Enrichment of Bank Statement Items" feature directly addresses the time-consuming and manual task of reconciling bank statements. This enhancement, part of the SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition 2608 release, provides a powerful automation capability that intelligently identifies and assigns the correct business partner—be it a customer or a supplier—to each bank statement item during the import process. This enrichment paves the way for a more streamlined reconciliation by ensuring transactions are correctly linked to the corresponding accounts from the outset.

The primary benefit of this innovation is a substantial increase in automation, leading to a more efficient and accurate reconciliation process. By minimizing manual intervention, your finance team can accelerate the financial close and focus on value-added analysis rather than repetitive tasks. Moreover, this feature offers remarkable flexibility, empowering users to define their own custom rules for deriving business partner accounts. This adaptability ensures that the automation can be tailored to your specific business scenarios and banking formats, leading to a highly accurate and reliable reconciliation process

Enhancements to Matching Algorithms

In the realm of finance, reconciling bank statements is a critical task, and the new **Enhancements to Matching Algorithms** in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition are designed to significantly advance the automation of this process. Simply put, these enhancements make the system smarter and more flexible when matching incoming payments to open invoices. New capabilities, such as "period aggregation matching," allow the system to reconcile a single payment against a group of open items that span different financial periods. Furthermore, the system now supports general ledger (G/L) items in its allocation logic and includes a "unique match switch," which instructs the system to only perform an automatic clearing if it finds exactly one perfect match, preventing potential errors.

The primary benefit of these enhanced algorithms is a marked increase in both flexibility and automation coverage for your bank reconciliation process. By empowering the system to understand and process more complex payment structures, you can significantly reduce the number of items requiring manual review, leading to higher straight-through processing rates and freeing up your finance professionals for more strategic work. Moreover, these enhancements provide more controlled and precise clearing behavior, which builds greater trust in the automated system. The new "unique match switch," for example, minimizes the risk of incorrect postings by restricting automation to unambiguous cases. This level of control ensures that while you are increasing automation, you are also improving accuracy and strengthening internal financial controls, leading to a more efficient and reliable financial close.

Editable email body in Create Correspondence app

Effective communication is key to maintaining strong relationships with customers and suppliers. The `Create Correspondence` SAP Fiori app has been enhanced to provide greater flexibility in your outbound communications. Users can now fully edit and format the body of the email that accompanies a correspondence PDF. While the system pre-populates the email from a template, both the subject line and message text can be customized, with rich text formatting options including changes to font, color, size, and style.

This enhancement significantly improves the user experience by empowering your team to tailor messages to a specific business context. Instead of relying on rigid templates, users can add personal notes, clarify details, or highlight important information directly within the email before sending it. This flexibility reduces the need for follow-up emails or clarifications, minimizing repetitive work and ensuring that your communications are as clear and effective as possible.

Revenue Management 

Enabling Custom Fields for the Contract Account RAP Object

A core requirement for modern businesses is the ability to adapt enterprise software to unique operational needs. With the 2608 release, we are introducing advanced extensibility for the contract account business object. This feature allows for the addition of custom fields directly within the Manage Contract Accounts Fiori app, utilizing the ABAP RESTful Application Programming Model (RAP). This enhancement caters to both key users, who can implement custom logic without deep technical expertise, and developers, who can address more complex scenarios using predefined extension points in ABAP development tools.

The primary benefit of this innovation is the enhanced adaptability it provides. Your organization can now tailor the contract account to capture specific data points crucial to your business processes, directly improving data relevance and utility. Furthermore, by providing configurable extension points for core nodes and events, this feature significantly reduces development effort and complexity. Most importantly, these extensions are designed to be stable and upgrade-compatible, ensuring that your customisations are preserved through future system updates, thereby protecting your investment and maintaining system integrity.

Managing Direct Debit Prenotifications in Contract Accounting

Efficiently managing payment processes is critical for maintaining healthy cash flow and customer relationships. This application provides a centralized and consolidated view of all prenotifications, displaying their current status and associated details.
